Save as docs/measurement/receipts/YYYY-MM-DD-<handle>-<track>.json. track: demo | own-agent. date: YYYY-MM-DD of the attempt. facilitator: a handle only, no personal data. network: yes | no, whether the machine had internet access during the attempt; required yes for Track A and for uv tool install; checked once before the clock starts (protocol 2.7). coaching_events: list of {"at", "what"}. failures: list of {"at", "milestone", "what"}, kept even when the attempt failed.

machine._comment: os and cpu as reported by the system (e.g. uname -sr, CPU model and core count); python and uv are `python3 --version` and `uv --version`. uv_cache: cold (fresh UV_CACHE_DIR) or warm.

package._comment: version: the agent-reliability-ci version installed. source: pypi or wheel. wheel_sha256: required when source is wheel (record UV_FIND_LINKS and any UV_CACHE_DIR in notes, protocol 2.3). readme_url: the README read, at a fixed commit.

project._comment: Track B only; null for demo. kind: own | sample. description: what the agent is, or which recipe the sample tree came from. refs_preexisting: baseline, candidate, toolset and oracle were importable before the clock started. workers: worker count of the run.

timestamps._comment: ISO 8601 with timezone, e.g. 2026-10-20T09:15:02Z. Track A uses readme_opened, command_start, demo_banner, demo_verdict, all_steps_held, interpretation_answered. Track B uses readme_opened, install_start, install_done, scaffold_start, descriptor_written, run_start, verdict_printed, store_validated, interpretation_answered. Leave the others null.

durations_seconds._comment: Whole seconds derived from the timestamps as the protocol defines per track (sections 3 and 4). agent_execution is Track B only: the sum of usage.wall_seconds over trials.jsonl in the run store (protocol 4.2), never subtracted from total.

outcome._comment: completed: every stop condition of the track held. verdict: PASS | BLOCK | INCONCLUSIVE | ERROR; Track B: the verdict stamped as verdict_printed; ERROR if none; Track A: the verdict for agent B. store_validated, decision_sha256, init_attempts, descriptor_hand_edited, trials_started: Track B only (protocol 4.3 and 4.6). descriptor_hand_edited: arci.yaml edited by hand before the run that produced the verdict, or, with no valid verdict, before any arci run that started trials. trials_started: trials.jsonl in the run store (protocol 4.2) exists and is non-empty. interpretation_correct is scored with the key in protocol 5.3.
outcome.verdict: VERDICT: BLOCK (exit 1)   [A vs agent_b]; passed under the fault: A 192/200, agent_b 132/200; matches the recorded run
outcome.interpretation_answer: With 200 trials per arm under a timeout on the first reserve call, agent B (agent A with the retry removed) succeeded 132/200 against A's 192/200. The upper bound on the difference in success rate was below -delta (-0.10), so the gate concludes B is worse than A by more than the allowed margin, and the check fails with exit 1. A single clean run (step 1) hid this, because both looked the same there.

comprehension._comment: Answered once per reader, on the first track's receipt; on a second-track receipt set answered_on to that file name and leave the rest empty. Answers verbatim; scores per the key in protocol section 5; scorer is not the reader and is a handle only, no personal data. q2_who_for keeps its name for schema stability; it holds the whole q2 answer (who it is for and what the agent must expose).

answers.q1_what_is_it: ARCI is a CLI and Python library that runs a baseline and a candidate version of an agent many times on the same predeclared task with seeded, injected tool faults. It grades each trial with an independent oracle over the final environment state and returns PASS/BLOCK/INCONCLUSIVE/ERROR as exit code 0/1/2/3. It works like a statistical regression gate for CI, and it can also diff, minimise and replay a recorded failure offline.
answers.q2_who_for: It is for engineers who change an agent (prompt, retry policy, model, code) and want CI to catch a reliability regression before merging. A Python agent must be an importable plain function agent(task, tools, rng) -> dict that does all its tool calls through tools.call(...). You also need a toolset factory (task, seed) -> object with .tools and .snapshot() and an oracle (task, final_state) -> bool. A non-Python agent can instead be a command that speaks MCP over stdio, so ARCI's boundary sees every tool call.
answers.q3_pass_means: PASS means that for this one predeclared experiment (task, faults, seeds, N, alpha, delta), the evidence supports that the candidate's success rate is not lower than the baseline's by more than delta. Concretely, the lower bound on candidate minus baseline is above -delta. It is relative non-inferiority, not a claim that either agent is reliable in absolute terms.
answers.q4_does_not_do: It is not a sandbox or security boundary: Python agents share a process with the boundary, and a hostile agent could forge or bypass its records. It only sees calls through its tool boundary, not direct files, network or subprocesses. It replays the recorded boundary, not the model, so a live model's bundle usually replays as INVALID. Also, declaring a fault does not guarantee it fires if the agent never calls that tool.
answers.q5_first_three_commands: 1) uv tool install agent-reliability-ci  2) arci init checkout-retry --baseline app.v1:run --candidate app.v2:run --toolset tests.world:make_world --oracle tests.world:passed (for this project I also needed --task '{"order_id": "order-7"}', and I added --fault tool_timeout:reserve:0)  3) arci run arci.yaml

q1: The answer covers baseline vs candidate, repeated runs on the same predeclared task with seeded injected faults, and a CI-gate verdict that names PASS and BLOCK.

q2: It names engineers changing an agent who want to catch a regression before merge. It also names both integration routes: the Python function agent(task, tools, rng) and a command that speaks MCP over stdio.

q3: It says PASS is relative to the baseline, non-inferiority within delta (lower bound above -delta), limited to this one predeclared experiment, and not a claim of absolute reliability.

q4: It gives several distinct README limits. The ones that count are that it is not a sandbox or security boundary, that it sees only calls across its tool boundary, and that it replays the boundary rather than the model.

q5: The three commands are in order: uv tool install agent-reliability-ci, then arci init with --baseline, --candidate, --toolset and --oracle, then arci run arci.yaml.

Demo-block interpretation (BLOCK): It says the candidate is worse than the baseline by more than the allowed margin, and it ties this to the stated conditions (200 trials per arm, timeout on the first reserve call). The upper bound of the difference below -delta supports it. It does not say "this experiment" in those words, but the scoping is explicit enough.

Own-run interpretation: The verdict line was INCONCLUSIVE (exit 2), and the answer matches it. It says the gate can neither show non-inferiority nor claim a regression, that the sample is too small, that this does not mean v2 is safe, and that arci plan is the way to size a larger run.
